paragraphs.text: Dormandy (1957) described Peutz-Jeghers syndrome as gastrointestinal polyposis with mucocutaneous pigmentation. Giardiello et al. (1987) and Jenne et al. (1998) described it as an autosomal dominant disorder with hamartomatous polyps of the gastrointestinal tract and mucocutaneous melanin deposits or melanocytic macules of the lips. Hemminki et al. (1997) noted that the melanin spots involve the lips, buccal mucosa, and digits. They also noted a greatly increased risk of malignancy, including gastrointestinal tumors and cancers of the breast, ovary, testis, and uterine cervix. Mehenni et al. (1997) likewise noted an increased frequency of gastrointestinal and extraintestinal malignancies, and Hemminki et al. (1998) described PJS as a rare hereditary disease that predisposes to benign and malignant tumors in many organ systems.

paragraphs.text: Cantu et al. (1980) described a 6-year-old boy with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and a unilateral feminizing Sertoli cell tumor. Plasma and urine estrogen levels were consistently high, and testosterone and dihydrotestosterone levels were normal. The raised estrogen levels did not change after exogenous gonadotropin administration, which indicated autonomous production. Histology of the nontumorous testicular tissue suggested that the estrogens may have had both stimulating and atrophying effects on the seminiferous tubules. The authors concluded that gonadal tumors are an additional manifestation of the Peutz-Jeghers syndrome gene in both males and females.

paragraphs.text: Entius et al. (2001) analyzed 39 polyps and 5 carcinomas from 17 PJS patients in 13 families. They found LOH at 19p13.3 in 15 of the 39 hamartomatous polyps and in all 5 carcinomas. The authors concluded that STK11 acts as a tumor suppressor and may be involved early in PJS tumorigenesis, and suggested that future work test whether LOH in polyps could serve as a biomarker to predict cancer. In the carcinomas there was no LOH at 5q, but 4 of 5 had APC mutations. There was no 17p LOH and no p53 mutation. One carcinoma had an activating KRAS codon 12 mutation, and another had 18q LOH without loss of SMAD4 expression. The authors suggested that these differences from the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence point to a distinct pathway of carcinogenesis.
